assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3 and S1, S2, S3 are encoded as discrete events rather than persistent input variables, following the NL trigger wording.
hbrg is encoded as an integer output with 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stop.

Outstanding request context is not modeled as memory variables because the NL listed direct floor/request transitions and did not specify request latching or arbitration beyond immediate next-destination checking at floor states.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init: dispatches to floor 1 stopped, then PS2 drives upward to MU2, S2 stops at F2, PS3 immediately drives upward to MU3, and S3 stops at F3.
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_up_to_f2_then_f3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from F1, PS3 must target MU3 exactly and S3 must complete arrival at F3 with stop output.
scenario_results.name: f1_request_f3_direct_up_path

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from F2, PS1 must target MD1 exactly with downward drive, and S1 must complete arrival at F1 stopped.
scenario_results.name: f2_request_f1_down_path

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from F3, PS2 must target MD2 exactly with downward drive, and S2 must complete arrival at F2 stopped.
scenario_results.name: f3_request_f2_down_path

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from F3, PS1 must target MD1 exactly with downward drive, and S1 must complete arrival at F1 stopped.
scenario_results.name: f3_request_f1_down_path

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: reset from an upward travel state must force F1 regardless of motion/request context and set stop output.
scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_up_motion

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: reset from a downward travel state must force F1 regardless of motion/request context and set stop output.
scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_down_motion

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: while moving upward to F2, an unrelated S1 arrival sensor must not complete the MU2 motion transition.
scenario_results.name: wrong_arrival_sensor_does_not_complete_motion

evidence: NL requires floor states F1/F2/F3 and motion states MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL defines all seven leaf states.
NL specifies F1->MU2 on PS2, F1->MU3 on PS3, F2->MU3 on PS3, F2->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD1 on PS1, and F3->MD2 on PS2; DSL contains these transitions exactly.
NL specifies MU2+S2->F2, MU3+S3->F3, MD1+S1->F1, and MD2+S2->F2; DSL contains these transitions exactly.
NL states hbrg distinguishes upward drive, downward drive, and stop; DSL sets hbrg=1 in MU states, hbrg=-1 in MD states, and hbrg=0 in floor states.
NL states reset forces floor 1 regardless of context; DSL includes forced transition ! * -> F1 :: reset.
findings.summary: The DSL is faithful to the stated elevator FSM: it includes the required floor states, motion states, request-triggered departures, arrival-sensor completions, stop/up/down hbrg outputs, initial F1 state, and reset-to-F1 behavior.

evidence: GroundingMap marks all required states, hbrg actions, request events, sensor events, initial transition, motion transitions, and reset transition as required with high confidence.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 11 normal transitions, 7 forced reset expansions, 7 events, 1 variable, and 7 actions.
sim_summary reports 8/8 scenarios passed, including upward travel, downward travel, direct floor requests, reset from motion states, and ignoring a wrong arrival sensor.
findings.summary: Required model components are covered at a candidate/reference-review level: states, events, transitions, actions, and output variable are all grounded and exercised by simulation.

evidence: sim_summary includes reset_from_mu3_lands_f1 and reset_from_md2_lands_f1 but does not show reset from F1/F2/F3 in the sample.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports n_transitions_forced=7 for reset, supporting broad reset coverage despite limited sampled reset scenarios.
findings.summary: Scenario coverage is adequate for the explicit NL transition set; no blocking coverage gap is evident. The only minor residual is that reset from floor states is not shown in the sampled simulations, although the forced reset transition expands across all leaf states by inspection.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary has blocking_count=0 and one advisory W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for hbrg.
NL describes hbrg as an output that distinguishes drive/stop conditions, not as an input or decision variable.
DSL writes hbrg in state enter actions and never uses it in guards, which is consistent with an output-only role.
findings.summary: The W_UNREFERENCED_VAR diagnostic for hbrg is advisory and expected because hbrg is modeled as a pure output rather than an internal guard variable.

evidence: No parse, semantic, or design blocking errors are reported.
GroundingMap provides high-confidence evidence for all required states, transitions, events, and hbrg actions.
sim_summary reports all 8 scenarios passed.
The model is not an empty shell or label-only state model; it has concrete transitions and state-entry output actions.
findings.summary: No NFRR quality cap is warranted. Estimated tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate, because the model has high NL fidelity, required components are present, diagnostics are nonblocking, and scenario tests cover the explicit transition behavior.
